notes:
First daf of the Phase 3 evidence-backed correction queue, and the only SHIFTED daf in the corpus. Diagnosis before editing: the corpus semantic audit ranked 7a highest (score 10.0), the drift classifier reported SHIFTED with anchors 3 found / 1 missing at offsets -4, -4, -11, and the packet carried the explicit WARNING that stub repair and link edits are forbidden here. rashi-realignment is therefore the classifier's own recommended remedy, which is what this manifest carries.

The defect was shifted-compression, not fabrication: genuine, mostly accurate translations existed but had been packed into roughly the first sixteen entries and then re-stated three more times over (entries 17-23, 24-41, 42-53 each restate material already covered), so no entry translated the raw print line it was attached to. That is exactly why the citation anchors trailed their Hebrew by 4 and 11 lines.

Rebuilt all 53 entries so each one translates only its own raw print line, re-extracting the raw Hebrew fresh from the packet and mapping every line before writing any English. Content covers: the Numbers 9 derivation that corpse impurity is permitted for a community but an individual is deferred to the second Pesach, with the counter-list of bodily impurities that were never permitted (l01, lines 1-4); Rav Nachman's concession where remainders are eaten, resting on the rule that a communal offering offered in impurity is still not eaten in impurity, cited to Pesachim 77b (l06, lines 4-9); the objection from the minchah of bulls, rams, and lambs of the Festival, whose time is fixed (l08, l11, lines 9-14); Rav Nachman's three-part reply distinguishing the idolatry bull, Aaron's Yom Kippur ram, and the lamb accompanying the omer, with the Leviticus 23 citation and the point that the 'minchah of lambs' means the omer's own minchah rather than the wholly-burned libation minchah (l12, lines 14-23); the blood-thrown-intentionally case and the rabbinic penalty that still leaves the owners atoned (l17, lines 23-28); the long tzitz sugya on what the frontplate effects acceptance for, the force of 'willingly' alongside 'under compulsion', and the individual/community distinction regarding bodily impurity (l19, lines 28-41); Rav Nachman's reading that the tzitz clause speaks of an individual while the community clause speaks only of fitness (l23, lines 42-45); and the piggul/notar elimination that leaves impurity as the only sin the tzitz can address, with the Zevachim 28a citation (l26, lines 45-52).

Seven raw lines are genuine dibbur-boundary straddles where one comment closes and the next opens inside the same print line (lines 4, 9, 10, 14, 23, 28, 45). audit_rashi_association.py --range-from 7a --range-to 7a reports declared_associations=60 = 46*1 + 7*2, matching the hand prediction exactly, with 0 broken and 0 cross-daf.

One bounded correction was made during the edit, before any verification failed. The first pass rendered the Pesachim citation split across English lines 6 and 7 to mirror the Hebrew print break, which left the daf-number anchor at offset +1: the anchor scanner's splitContinuation rule sources the digits from the following Hebrew line but attributes the citation to line 6, so the English has to carry the whole citation on line 6 to land at offset 0. Rendering '(Pesachim 77b)' complete on line 6 is also the more faithful English, since the split is an artifact of the print column, not of the citation. After that adjustment all four anchors sit at offset 0.

Post-edit evidence, all re-run on the final tree: classification ALIGNED (was SHIFTED), lineLevelSafe true, 4 anchors found (was 3), 0 missing (was 1), offsets [0, 0, 0, 0], maxAbsOffset 0 - the multi-anchor-safe tier, so no attestation block is required. audit_rashi_scaffold.py 7a --no-baseline: 0 hits. No scaffold-baseline, repetition-baseline, or content-allowlist entry existed for 7a before or after. l02 is confirmed to receive no Rashi comment: after the l01 comment Rashi's next dibbur is Rav Nachman's 'modina' (l06), and the 'and if there is only it' lemma he explains next belongs to the l08 braita that repeats it, which is the reading consistent with Rashi's own daf order. Entry count and vilnaLine sequence are unchanged at 53, matching the talmuddev raw lines exactly; no structural or count change was made or needed.
